summary: Cooldown window causes temporary unpin and fallback during canary synchronization
description: Issue summary: During a canary sync for NovaChat's dedicated pool, a background cooldown timer on the pin-commit path caused some tenant sessions to lose their explicit model pin briefly, resulting in fallbacks to a degraded variant for ~30-90s. Impact: Several customer requests (approx 2.3k requests over the window) returned responses from fallback variant with slightly different tokenization and higher latency. Environment: prod-us-east, NovaChat dedicated pool (pool-id: dc-118), model redwood-v2.1-base pinned at route /chat/generate. Observed behaviour appears tied to the pin-commit cooldown interaction with canary state reconciliation and edge prewarm probes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Ensure tenant is pinned to redwood-v2.1-base on dedicated pool dc-118
2) Trigger a staged canary sync that updates routing snapshot across edge nodes (simulate our canary roll script with --stagger=5s)
3) Observe pin-commit flow and cooldown timer on orchestrator during snapshot merge
4) Reproduce by replaying customer traffic while forcing an orchestrator snapshot re-election
5) Check routing responses for model_variant header and compare latency/tokenization differences

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: cooldown logic on pin-commit prevents immediate re-affirmation of explicit pins when snapshot version increments rapidly, allowing routing fallthrough to fallback priority list.

Observed that cooldown_ms default (15000) plus staggered snapshot merges created a window where some edge nodes served from local stale route table that did not include the latest pin commit, so routing fell back to model variant with lower precedence.
KV cache mismatch logs indicate session rebinds to degraded variant rather than true unpin (pin existed but commit path blocked by cooldown check).
Edge probe timings correlate: nodes that processed prewarm probes during cooldown had higher probability of serving degraded variant.
comments: Support (Aisha): Customer reported intermittent lower-quality responses and slight latency increases during today's scheduled canary. They saw mismatch in tokenization on 2-3% of calls.
SRE (Diego): Reproduced locally by fast snapshot merges; orchestration logs show cooldown prevented pin commit handshake. Creating a small test to vary cooldown_ms.

Engineering (Maya Chen): Looking at pin-commit state machine. Possible quick fix: skip cooldown on explicit pin-commit originating from control-plane during canary syncs, but need to evaluate race against thrashing protection.
Customer (NovaChat - Samir Rao): Impacted an ongoing internal demo. Appreciate ETA on mitigation.
workaround: Manual hold: temporarily pause edge prewarm probes for NovaChat's dedicated pool until we deploy a targeted fix. Alternatively, set a transient higher canary-stagger window so snapshot merges do not overlap with pin-commit cooldowns.
next_steps: 1) Short-term: Apply orchestration config to exempt control-plane-originated pin commits from cooldown for affected pools (rollback safe), target deploy 2026-03-13 03:00 UTC
2) Medium-term: Update pin-commit state machine to use explicit commit TTLs tied to snapshot epochs so commits survive rapid re-elections without falling through to fallback list
3) Add observability: metric pin_commit_skipped_by_cooldown{tenant,pool} and dashboard alert threshold
4) Run a controlled canary with NovaChat after fix and monitor for mixed-variant responses for 1 hour
